title: Build a Layout with Flexbox
description: Master 1-dimensional CSS Flexbox layout: control main and cross axes, distribute items with justify-content, align with align-items, and build real-world navigation and modal components.

objectives.statement: Understand flex containers, flex items, and the distinction between main and cross axes established by flex-direction.
Distribute and align elements along main and cross axes using justify-content and align-items.
Implement responsive navigation bars and centered modal overlay layouts using standard Flexbox properties.

content.title: Build a Layout with Flexbox
content.hook: Centering an element or building responsive navigation once required complex floats and table hacks. Flexbox introduced a predictable, one-dimensional layout model.
content.context: Modern UI development relies on CSS Flexible Box Layout (Flexbox) to dynamically distribute space, align content across directional axes, and build resilient components.
goals: Differentiate between flex containers and flex items
Master main axis vs cross axis orientation controlled by flex-direction
Control spatial distribution with justify-content and alignment with align-items
Construct real-world UI components including responsive navbars and centered modal backdrops

content.title: Flexbox Architecture: Containers, Axes, and Alignment
content.text:
When you declare display: flex on an element, it becomes a flex container and its direct children become flex items.

Flexbox operates along two orthogonal axes:
1. Main Axis: The primary direction items flow, governed by flex-direction (defaults to row, flowing left-to-right).
2. Cross Axis: Perpendicular to the main axis (defaults to top-to-bottom in row mode).

Alignment properties target specific axes:
- justify-content aligns items along the MAIN axis (e.g., flex-start, center, flex-end, space-between, space-around, space-evenly).
- align-items aligns items along the CROSS axis (e.g., stretch, center, flex-start, flex-end, baseline).

callout.text: Remember: justify-content ALWAYS aligns along the main axis. If flex-direction: column is applied, the main axis becomes vertical, meaning justify-content controls vertical distribution and align-items controls horizontal alignment!

content.keyTakeaway: justify-content governs the main axis; align-items governs the cross axis. The main axis direction is defined by flex-direction.

content.title: Visualizing Flexbox Axes & Space Distribution
content.description: An architectural visualization demonstrating a flex container in row mode. The horizontal main axis is governed by justify-content: space-between, pushing the first and last child to opposite edges. The vertical cross axis is governed by align-items: center, vertically aligning items along the container's center line.

content.prompt: Predict the exact visual layout produced by the following CSS declarations applied to a navigation header container:
options: Items are distributed evenly across the horizontal main axis with the first and last items flush against the edges, and vertically centered along the cross axis
Items are tightly grouped in the horizontal center with no spacing between them, and aligned to the top edge
Items are stacked vertically from top to bottom with equal space between them, and centered horizontally
Items are pushed completely to the right edge horizontally, and stretched to fill the full height of 64px
content.explanation: With flex-direction: row, the main axis is horizontal. justify-content: space-between distributes available space between items, pushing the outer items flush to the left and right edges. align-items: center vertically centers the items along the 64px cross axis.

validation.expected: Items are distributed evenly across the horizontal main axis with the first and last items flush against the edges, and vertically centered along the cross axis

hints.content: Identify the main axis: with flex-direction: row (or default), the main axis runs horizontally.
What does justify-content: space-between do on the main axis? It places equal space between items, pushing the first and last items to the edges.
What does align-items: center do on the cross axis? It centers the items vertically across the container height.

feedback.correct: Spot on! In row orientation, justify-content: space-between distributes items edge-to-edge horizontally and align-items: center centers them vertically.
feedback.incorrect: Remember: In row mode, the main axis is horizontal (justify-content: space-between spreads items to edges) and the cross axis is vertical (align-items: center centers items vertically).

content.title: Interactive Flexbox Workshop: Build Navbar & Modal Overlay
content.prompt: Complete the two essential UI layout tasks in the CSS editor for the navbar and modal backdrop.
content.instructions:
Complete the two essential UI layout tasks in the CSS editor:

1. Navigation Bar (.navbar):
   - Set display to flex to establish a flex formatting context.
   - Distribute items to the outer edges using justify-content: space-between.
   - Vertically center items along the cross axis using align-items: center.

2. Modal Backdrop (.modal-backdrop):
   - Set display to flex.
   - Horizontally center the modal dialog using justify-content: center.
   - Vertically center the modal dialog using align-items: center.

hints.content: To activate Flexbox layout on .navbar and .modal-backdrop, add 'display: flex;' to both rules.
On .navbar, add 'justify-content: space-between;' to spread items edge-to-edge, and 'align-items: center;' to vertically center them.
On .modal-backdrop, add 'justify-content: center;' and 'align-items: center;' to achieve perfect 2-axis centering.

feedback.correct: Outstanding! You have successfully implemented standard Flexbox patterns for both the navigation bar and the centered modal backdrop.
feedback.incorrect: Ensure .navbar has display: flex, justify-content: space-between, and align-items: center, and .modal-backdrop has display: flex, justify-content: center, and align-items: center.

content.title: Flexbox Layout Mastery: Synthesis & Key Takeaways
content.summary: You have mastered 1-dimensional CSS layout mechanics using Flexbox.
takeaways: Flex Containers vs Items: Setting display: flex establishes a flex formatting context for immediate children.
Main vs Cross Axes: The main axis is determined by flex-direction (row by default). The cross axis runs perpendicular.
Main Axis Distribution: justify-content controls alignment and spacing along the main axis (flex-start, center, flex-end, space-between, space-around, space-evenly).
Cross Axis Alignment: align-items controls alignment across the cross axis (stretch, center, flex-start, flex-end, baseline).

Common UI Patterns: Combining justify-content: space-between with align-items: center powers navigation bars, while dual centering with justify-content: center and align-items: center creates modal overlays.
